Privacy Policy

Effective Date: October 18, 2026. How Cargoline processes and protects enterprise freight information and user identity data.

1. Information We Collect

Cargoline collects commercial logistics data necessary to fulfill shipment tracking and visibility services, including container numbers, master air waybill identifiers, origin and destination port codes, carrier EDI milestone transmissions, and commercial invoice line item totals submitted for landed cost calculations.

2. Use of Logistics Data

Customer shipment data is used strictly to provide real-time container tracking, calculate predictive arrival windows, generate automated demurrage risk ledgers, and synchronize milestone records into customer ERP and TMS software. Customer data is never monetized or shared with third-party advertising networks.

3. Data Confidentiality & Tenant Partitioning

All operational shipment manifests and tariff calculations are logically isolated using Row-Level Security database controls. Carrier contract rates and freight expense details are cryptographically protected and inaccessible to other organizations utilizing the platform.

4. International Data Transfers & Compliance

Cargoline adheres to the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the UK GDPR, and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA). Enterprise customers may execute our standard Data Processing Addendum (DPA) incorporating European Commission Standard Contractual Clauses.

5. Contact Our Data Protection Officer

Inquiries regarding privacy practices or data processing agreements should be directed to our compliance team at privacy@cargoline.io or through our contact sales interface.

Cargoline Technical Security Architecture
VERSION 4.2 • APPROVED
1. Executive Summary & Scope

Cargoline processes commercial freight shipping manifests, vessel telemetry, customs entry data, and purchase order identifiers on behalf of mid-market and enterprise importing organizations. This document details the technical and administrative controls implemented across the software lifecycle to preserve data integrity and prevent unauthorized disclosure.

2. Encryption Architecture

Data transmission between customer web browsers, API clients, carrier gateways, and Cargoline application clusters is strictly restricted to TLS 1.3 encryption. Older protocols (TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1) are explicitly rejected at network edge routers.

All persistent data stores, database volumes, backups, and message queues are encrypted at rest using AES-256 with keys managed through hardware security modules (HSM) certified under FIPS 140-2 Level 3. Encryption keys undergo automated cryptographic rotation every 90 days.

3. Data Segregation & Tenant Boundaries

Customer data is logically partitioned utilizing database Row-Level Security (RLS) policies. Every application query carries authenticated tenant context. Container records, bills of lading, and tariff classifications belonging to one importer are cryptographically segregated and completely inaccessible to other platform participants.

4. Incident Response & Business Continuity

Cargoline maintains warm cross-region database replicas with automated failover capabilities. The Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is under 5 minutes, and the Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is under 60 minutes for core tracking telemetry pipelines. External penetration tests are executed annually by CREST-accredited testing firms.

Local storage

Your choices

Before production

A real shop needs an identified data controller, lawful processing basis, retention schedule and a way to exercise privacy rights. This demonstration does not establish those arrangements.
